---
title: "05 – Does S. aureus phosphorylate histidine?"
subtitle: "Bio253 HS2026 · STY vs STYH search, judged conservatively"
---

**Claim to test:** Prust *et al.* 2021 (*Mol Cell Proteomics* 20:100034) report that
~8 % of all *S. aureus* phospho-sites are on **histidine** (pHis). Can we see pHis
in our data – and how sure can we be?

The raw files were searched twice:

* **STY** – phosphorylation allowed on Ser, Thr, Tyr
* **STYH** – additionally on His

::: {.callout-important}
## Be sceptical – on purpose
* pHis is **acid-labile**. Our workflow (Fe-IMAC enrichment, acidic LC) is not
  pHis-friendly, so many pHis may be lost – and the ones we "see" need extra scrutiny.
* The main source of false pHis is **mis-localisation**: if a peptide also contains
  S, T or Y, the search engine may put the phosphate on H although it sits on a
  neighbour – or the other way round.
* Allowing H as an extra acceptor makes the search space bigger, which by itself
  creates some extra (false) hits.

We therefore treat pHis **very conservatively**. You will build evidence tiers yourself.
:::


```{r setup}

library(ggrepel)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readxl)
library(here)
source("../R/setup.R")
# keep contaminants here: we want the complete peptide lists of both searches
styh <- read_sites("STYH", drop_contaminants = FALSE)
sty  <- read_sites("STY",  drop_contaminants = FALSE)
total_prot <- readxl::read_xlsx(
  here::here("data/raw/total", "DE_total.xlsx"),
  sheet = "normalized_abundances",
  col_types = "text"
) %>%
  dplyr::select(protein_Id, protein_length) %>%
  dplyr::distinct() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    protein_length = as.numeric(protein_length)
  )
head(total_prot)
summary(total_prot$protein_length)
```

```{r residues}
bind_rows(styh, sty) |>

styh |>
```

**Question:** the STYH search finds more sites in total. Are the additional sites
only His sites, or do S/T/Y counts also change? Why might they?

## 2. Localisation probability

`best_loc_prob` = best localisation probability of a site over all samples
(1 = the search engine is sure the phosphate sits on exactly this residue).

```{r lp-distribution, fig.height=4}
site_level <- distinct(styh, site_id, residue, best_loc_prob)

ggplot(site_level, aes(best_loc_prob, colour = residue)) +
  stat_ecdf(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.75, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "best localisation probability", y = "fraction of sites with LP <= x",
       title = "STYH search: localisation probability per residue")

site_level |>
  mutate(lp_class = lp_class(best_loc_prob)) |>
  count(residue, lp_class) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = lp_class, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
```

**Question:** Are His sites localised as well as S/T/Y sites? How many His sites
have LP ≥ 0.75?

## 3. One evidence table for every His site

We now collect, for every His site, the evidence we need. Read each step.

### 3a. Sites, localisation and reproducibility

**Reproducibility is judged from the intensity** (detected = intensity > 0), not from
the per-sample localisation probabilities: FragPipe sometimes reports an LP for a
sample in which the site was *not quantified*.

```{r lp-filled}
styh |>
  filter(residue == "H") |>
  summarise(sample_rows = n(),
            quantified = sum(!is.na(intensity)),
            LP_reported_but_not_quantified = sum(is.na(intensity) & loc_prob_fragpipe > 0,
                                                 na.rm = TRUE))
```

```{r evidence-1}
his <- styh |>
  filter(residue == "H") |>
  group_by(site_id, locus_tag, product, peptide, best_loc_prob) |>
  summarise(
    n_samples_quant = sum(!is.na(intensity)),                  # of 27
    n_samples_lp075 = sum(loc_prob_fragpipe >= 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),  # FragPipe LPs, for reference only
    max_reps_in_group = max(tapply(!is.na(intensity), group, sum)),  # best group, of 3
    .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(lp_class = lp_class(best_loc_prob))
nrow(his)
```

### 3b. Is there an alternative acceptor on the peptide?

If the peptide contains **no S, T or Y at all**, the phosphate cannot be
mis-placed onto a neighbouring S/T/Y. That is the strongest kind of evidence we can
get from the search alone. A `Peptide` entry can contain several sequence variants
separated by `;` – we take the variant with the fewest S/T/Y.

```{r evidence-2}
peptide_variants("ANhEQIIEAIK;MANhEQIIEAIK")   # example: two variants, upper-cased
n_sty_acceptors("ANhEQIIEAIK;MANhEQIIEAIK")

his <- his |>
  mutate(n_sty_acceptors = n_sty_acceptors(peptide),
         no_alt_acceptor = n_sty_acceptors == 0,
         co_phospho_STY  = co_phospho_sty(peptide))
count(his, no_alt_acceptor)
```

### 3c. Does the STY-only search explain the same peptide?

If the very same peptide was also identified as a phosphopeptide in the STY search,
the spectrum can be explained **without** pHis. FragPipe writes phospho residues in
lower case, so we compare upper-cased sequences. We count a His peptide as
"explained" only if **all** its variants appear in the STY search.

```{r evidence-3}
sty_peptides <- phosphopeptide_set(sty)
his <- his |>
  mutate(seen_in_STY_search   = all_variants_in(peptide, sty_peptides),
         partly_in_STY_search = any_variant_in(peptide, sty_peptides))
count(his, no_alt_acceptor, seen_in_STY_search)
```

## 4. Worked example: HPr His15

HPr (phosphocarrier protein of the PTS sugar uptake system) carries a **textbook
pHis at His15** – the phosphate is transferred from enzyme I to HPr-His15 and on to
sugar transporters. If we find any real pHis, HPr should be a candidate.

```{r hpr-find}
hpr <- find_protein("B7H15_05615") |> select(locus_tag, product, protein_key, staa8_uniprot)
hpr
```

The same HPr peptide in the two searches:

```{r hpr-compare}
hpr_peptide <- "MEQNSYVIIDETGIHAR"
bind_rows(styh, sty) |>
  filter(protein_key %in% hpr$protein_key,
         str_detect(toupper(peptide), hpr_peptide)) |>
  group_by(search, site_id, residue, position, peptide, best_loc_prob) |>
  summarise(n_samples_quant = sum(!is.na(intensity)), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(search, position)
```

**Questions**

* In the STY search, where is the phosphate placed on this peptide? In STYH?
* Which interpretation is chemically / biologically more plausible, and why?
* Is the STY-search interpretation "wrong" – or simply the best it could do without H?
* Does this single example prove that pHis survives our workflow?

## 5. His sites on proteins that *should* carry pHis

Classical pHis proteins in bacteria: **histidine kinases** of two-component systems
(autophosphorylation on His, transfer to Asp of the response regulator – note:
pAsp was not searched), **HPr** and **enzyme I** of the PTS, and some metabolic
enzymes (e.g. succinyl-CoA synthetase, nucleoside-diphosphate kinase).

```{r canonical}
canonical_pattern <- "histidine kinase|phosphocarrier|PTS|phosphoenolpyruvate|response regulator|succinate--CoA|nucleoside-diphosphate kinase"
find_protein(canonical_pattern) |> count(product, sort = TRUE)

his |>
  filter(str_detect(product, regex(canonical_pattern, ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  select(locus_tag, product, site_id, peptide, best_loc_prob, n_sty_acceptors,
         seen_in_STY_search, max_reps_in_group)


## Define canonical phosphotransfer proteins
canonical_proteins <- find_protein(canonical_pattern) |>
  select(locus_tag) |>
  distinct()

## All proteins detected in the STYH search
all_proteins <- styh |>
  distinct(locus_tag)

## Identify canonical proteins
protein_tbl <- all_proteins |>
  mutate(
    canonical = locus_tag %in% canonical_proteins$locus_tag
  )

## Identify proteins with at least one pHis site
his_proteins <- his |>
  distinct(locus_tag) |>
  mutate(has_pHis = TRUE)

## Combine both datasets
protein_tbl <- protein_tbl |>
  left_join(his_proteins, by = "locus_tag") |>
  mutate(
    has_pHis = ifelse(is.na(has_pHis), FALSE, has_pHis)
  )

## Construct contingency table
tab <- table(
  factor(protein_tbl$canonical, levels = c(TRUE, FALSE)),
  factor(protein_tbl$has_pHis, levels = c(TRUE, FALSE)))
rownames(tab) <- c("Canonical", "Other proteins")
colnames(tab) <- c("pHis detected", "No pHis detected")
tab
## Fisher's exact test
fisher.test(tab, alternative = "greater")
```

**Question:** Do any histidine kinases show a His site? Is the site at the
conserved, autophosphorylated His (look at the protein in UniProt via
`staa8_uniprot`)? What about the many His sites on proteins that are *not* known
pHis proteins?

## 6. Your task: build confidence tiers

Combine the evidence into **tiers**, from "strongest candidate" to "unreliable".
Suggested criteria (you decide the order and thresholds – and justify them!):

| evidence | column |
|---|---|
| no alternative S/T/Y acceptor on the peptide | `no_alt_acceptor` |
| well localised | `best_loc_prob >= 0.75` |
| reproducible: ≥ 2 of 3 replicates in some group | `max_reps_in_group >= 2` |
| peptide **not** explained by the STY search | `!seen_in_STY_search` |

Write your tiers below (set `eval: true` once you filled in the conditions).
Number tiers 1 (strongest) to 6 (weakest) and **start every label with the number**.

```{r my-tiers}
#| eval: true


my_tiers <- his |>
  mutate(
    tier = case_when(
      no_alt_acceptor &
        best_loc_prob >= 0.75 &
        max_reps_in_group >= 2 &
        !seen_in_STY_search ~ "1 strongest",
      best_loc_prob >= 0.75 &
        max_reps_in_group >= 2 &
        !seen_in_STY_search ~ "2 very strong",
      no_alt_acceptor &
        best_loc_prob >= 0.75 ~ "3 strong",
      best_loc_prob >= 0.75 ~ "4 moderate",
      no_alt_acceptor ~ "5 weak",
      TRUE ~ "6 unreliable"))
count(my_tiers, tier)

#add plot

my_tiers |>
  count(tier) |>
  mutate(tier = factor(
    tier,
    levels = c(
      "1 strongest",
      "2 very strong",
      "3 strong",
      "4 moderate",
      "5 weak",
      "6 unreliable"
    )
  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(tier, n)) +
  geom_col() +
   geom_col(fill = "midnightblue") +
  labs(
    x = "Tier",
    y = "Number of sites",
    title = "His-site confidence tiers"
  ) + 
  theme_minimal()

```

Check your tiers against the lecturer's reference (counts only – it tells you
*how many* sites agree, not *which*):

```{r check}
#| eval: true
check_his_tiers(my_tiers)
```

Which are the strongest sites? 
The following sites fullfil all criteria of the strongest confidence tier: no alternative S/T/Y acceptor, localisation
probability ≥ 0.75, reproducible detection (≥ 2 replicates in one group), and not explained by the STY search (are located
in tier 1).

```{r}
my_tiers |>
  filter(tier == "1 strongest") |>
  select(
    site_id,
    locus_tag,
    product,
    peptide,
    best_loc_prob,
    max_reps_in_group)

```

according to  String, they are not linked in any way. They don't belong to an obvious pathway.



```{r}
my_tiers %>%
  filter(tier == "2 very strong") %>%
  distinct(site_id,locus_tag, product) %>%
  arrange(product)
```



## 6.1 is it random (histidine kinase annotated proteins)?
Possible histidine kinase annotated proteins (genome wide)

```{r}
find_protein("histidine kinase") |>
  select(locus_tag, product)

```

found in the dataset styh sites
```{r}
tcs <- find_protein("histidine kinase") |>
  select(locus_tag, product)

styh |>
  distinct(locus_tag) |>
  inner_join(tcs, by = "locus_tag")
```


Following a test is the phosphorilisation is random or not on histidine kinase annotated proteins(Fisher Test).
```{r}
##  define TCS-proteines 
tcs <- find_protein("histidine kinase") |>
  select(locus_tag) |>
  distinct()

## All proteins
all_proteins <- styh |>
  select(locus_tag) |>
  distinct() |>
  mutate(
    TCS = locus_tag %in% tcs$locus_tag
  )

## Proteines with at least one pHis
his_proteins <- his |>
  select(locus_tag) |>
  distinct() |>
  mutate(has_pHis = TRUE)

## put together
protein_tbl <- all_proteins |>
  left_join(his_proteins, by = "locus_tag") |>
  mutate(
    has_pHis = ifelse(is.na(has_pHis), FALSE, has_pHis)
  )

## 2x2-table
tab <- table(
  protein_tbl$TCS,
  protein_tbl$has_pHis
)

tab

## Fisher Exact Test
fisher.test(tab)

```
Six proteins annotated as histidine kinases (TCS proteins) were identified in the dataset. None contained a detected
histidine phosphosite. Consequently, the estimated odds ratio was 0. However, Fisher's exact test did not indicate a
significant association between TCS membership and the occurrence of histidine phosphosites (p = 0.193). Not really valuable
because only very few histidine kinase annotated proteins detected.

#6.2 more on the topic histidine kinases

Staphylococcus aureus is known to have 16 two-component systems  (doi: 10.3390/genes13010034)



```{r}

# ============================================================
# Histidine phosphorylation on histidine kinases
# Include sites regardless of localization probability
# ============================================================

# 1. Identify histidine kinase proteins by their annotation
hk_proteins <- styh %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    stringr::str_detect(
      stringr::str_to_lower(product),
      "histidine kinase|sensor kinase|two-component.*kinase"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(locus_tag, product)

# Inspect which histidine kinases were identified
hk_proteins

# 2. Extract histidine phosphorylation sites from these proteins
hk_his_sites <- styh %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    locus_tag %in% hk_proteins$locus_tag
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    residue = stringr::str_extract(
      site_id, "_[STYH](?=\\d+$)"
    ),
    residue = stringr::str_remove(residue, "^_"),
    position = as.numeric(
      stringr::str_extract(site_id, "\\d+$")
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(residue == "H")

# 3. Inspect all detected histidine sites on histidine kinases
# No localization probability filter is applied
hk_his_sites

# 4. Summarise evidence for each site
hk_his_summary <- hk_his_sites %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    site_id,
    locus_tag,
    product,
    peptide,
    position
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_samples_quant = sum(!is.na(intensity)),
    n_samples_lp075 = sum(
      loc_prob_fragpipe >= 0.75,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    n_samples_low_lp = sum(
      !is.na(loc_prob_fragpipe) &
        loc_prob_fragpipe < 0.75
    ),
    best_loc_prob = if (
      all(is.na(best_loc_prob))
    ) NA_real_ else max(best_loc_prob, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_reps_in_group = max(
      tapply(!is.na(intensity), group, sum)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    dplyr::desc(n_samples_quant)
  )

# 5. Display the summary
hk_his_summary

# 6. Count how many histidine kinase proteins and
#    histidine phosphorylation sites were found
nrow(hk_proteins)
dplyr::n_distinct(hk_his_summary$locus_tag)
nrow(hk_his_summary)

```


We can find 6 kinase annotations (same as in the segment 6.1) in our styh data (the rest might not have been detected). None of them were found to have any histidine-phosphorylated site(s).


Check for any phosphorilated sites on the detected histidine kinases:
```{r}

# Check all phosphorylation sites on the six histidine kinases,
# regardless of which amino acid is modified

hk_all_sites <- styh %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    locus_tag %in% hk_proteins$locus_tag
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    residue = stringr::str_extract(
      site_id, "_[STYH](?=\\d+$)"
    ),
    residue = stringr::str_remove(residue, "^_"),
    position = as.numeric(
      stringr::str_extract(site_id, "\\d+$")
    )
  )

# Count sites by residue type
hk_all_sites %>%
  dplyr::group_by(residue) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_sites = dplyr::n_distinct(site_id),
    n_measurements = sum(!is.na(intensity)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# List all sites, their localization probabilities and peptides
hk_all_sites %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    locus_tag,
    product,
    site_id,
    residue,
    position,
    peptide,
    best_loc_prob
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(locus_tag, position)

```

We found multiple phosphorilations on STY sites (in total 18 distinct sites)

Quick check, on which kinase are these sites located?

```{r}

# Summarise all phosphorylation sites on histidine kinases
hk_site_details <- hk_all_sites %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    locus_tag,
    product,
    residue,
    site_id,
    position,
    peptide
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    best_loc_prob = if (
      all(is.na(best_loc_prob))
    ) NA_real_ else max(best_loc_prob, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_samples_quant = sum(!is.na(intensity)),
    n_samples_lp075 = sum(
      loc_prob_fragpipe >= 0.75,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(locus_tag, residue, position)

hk_site_details

```

The most identified one is B7H15_11550 which has multiple phospho-sites close to 
each other so it might represent a multiple phosphorylated peptide region. Based on String it is involved in Potassium transport, ion transport and Two-component
regulatory system.

Interestingly no autophosphorilated histidine sites were detected on the kinases that were found.

Our 5 Tier1 proteins are outside of the usual canonical histidine-kinase category


```{r}
# 1. Define protein annotation patterns

canonical_pattern <- paste(
  "histidine kinase",
  "sensor kinase",
  "phosphocarrier",
  "PTS",
  "phosphoenolpyruvate",
  "response regulator",
  "two-component",
  "phosphorelay",
  "receiver domain",
  "succinate--CoA",
  "succinyl-CoA synthetase",
  "nucleoside-diphosphate kinase",
  "HPr",
  "enzyme I",
  sep = "|"
)

# More specific pattern for TCS-associated proteins
tcs_pattern <- paste(
  "histidine kinase",
  "sensor kinase",
  "response regulator",
  "two-component",
  "phosphorelay",
  "receiver domain",
  sep = "|"
)

# 2. Identify canonical pHis proteins

canonical_proteins <- find_protein(canonical_pattern) |>
  dplyr::distinct(locus_tag, product)

canonical_proteins

# 3. Identify TCS-associated proteins

tcs_proteins <- find_protein(tcs_pattern) |>
  dplyr::distinct(locus_tag, product)

tcs_proteins

# 4. Identify which proteins were detected in STYH

all_proteins <- styh |>
  dplyr::distinct(locus_tag)

canonical_detected <- canonical_proteins |>
  dplyr::inner_join(all_proteins, by = "locus_tag")

tcs_detected <- tcs_proteins |>
  dplyr::inner_join(all_proteins, by = "locus_tag")

# 5. Count annotated and detected proteins

data.frame(
  category = c("Canonical pHis proteins", "TCS-associated proteins"),
  annotated = c(
    nrow(canonical_proteins),
    nrow(tcs_proteins)),
  detected_in_STYH = c(
    nrow(canonical_detected),
    nrow(tcs_detected)))

# 6. Check all histidine sites on canonical proteins

canonical_his_sites <- styh |>
  dplyr::filter(
    locus_tag %in% canonical_detected$locus_tag
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    residue = stringr::str_extract(

    locus_tag, product, site_id, position, peptide

    best_loc_prob = if (all(is.na(best_loc_prob))) {

    } else {
      max(best_loc_prob, na.rm = TRUE)
    },
    n_samples_detected = sum(intensity > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_samples_lp075 = sum(
      loc_prob_fragpipe >= 0.75, na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(best_loc_prob)

canonical_his_sites

# 7. Check all histidine sites on TCS proteins

tcs_his_sites <- styh |>
```

```{r}
    n_samples_detected = sum(intensity > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_samples_lp075 = sum(
      loc_prob_fragpipe >= 0.75, na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(locus_tag, residue, position)

# Sites with localization probability below 0.75
tcs_low_probability <- tcs_all_sites |>
  dplyr::filter(
    is.na(best_loc_prob) | best_loc_prob < 0.75
  )

tcs_low_probability
```

how often in a specific group?
```{r}
# Summarise positive-intensity observations
# for the two response-regulator histidine sites

response_regulator_sites <- styh |>
  dplyr::filter(
    locus_tag %in% c("B7H15_03935", "B7H15_11300"),
    stringr::str_detect(site_id, "_H\\d+$")
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    locus_tag,
    product,
    site_id,
    peptide,
    best_loc_prob,
    group
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_detected = sum(intensity > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_intensity = sum(intensity, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(locus_tag, group)

response_regulator_sites
```

Two histidine phosphorylation candidates were found in proteins annotated as DNA-binding response regulators. The site H128 in B7H15_11300 (H128 site) had a localization probability of 0.7882, whereas H124 in B7H15_03935 had a probability of 0.3258. Both sites were detected with positive intensity in just one sample from the anc_SN group and were not detected in the other sample groups. -> Neither candidate showed sufficient reproducibility to be considered a high-confidence phosphorylation site.

B7H15_11300 (String) is involved in quorum sensing, signaling and cell comunication. FDR below 0.05 (statistically enriched in Stringnetwork)
Check how it stands against our categories for strong likelihood, that really the His is phophorylated.

```{r}

# Check B7H15_11300 H128 against the four Tier 1 criteria

candidate_site <- "lcl_CP020619.1_prot_ARG46599.1_2192_H128"

# 1. Get the histidine site and its peptide sequence
candidate_data <- styh |>
  dplyr::filter(site_id == candidate_site)

candidate_peptide <- candidate_data |>
  dplyr::distinct(peptide) |>
  dplyr::pull(peptide)

# 2. Check whether the peptide contains another S, T or Y
# The lowercase h marks the candidate phosphorylated histidine.
no_alt_acceptor <- !stringr::str_detect(
  stringr::str_to_upper(candidate_peptide),
  "[STY]"
)

# 3. Check the best localization probability
best_loc_prob <- max(
  candidate_data$best_loc_prob,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

# 4. Check reproducibility: count positive detections per group
group_detections <- candidate_data |>
  dplyr::group_by(group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_detected = sum(intensity > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

max_reps_in_group <- max(group_detections$n_detected)

# 5. Check whether the same peptide was found in the STY search
sty_peptides <- sty |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(peptide)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    peptide_key = stringr::str_to_upper(peptide)
  ) |>
  dplyr::distinct(peptide_key)

candidate_peptide_key <- stringr::str_to_upper(candidate_peptide)

seen_in_STY_search <- candidate_peptide_key %in%
  sty_peptides$peptide_key

# 6. Combine all four criteria
candidate_check <- tibble::tibble(
  locus_tag = "B7H15_11300",
  site_id = candidate_site,
  peptide = candidate_peptide,
  no_alt_acceptor = no_alt_acceptor,
  best_loc_prob = best_loc_prob,
  max_reps_in_group = max_reps_in_group,
  seen_in_STY_search = seen_in_STY_search
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    criterion_1 = no_alt_acceptor,
    criterion_2 = best_loc_prob >= 0.75,
    criterion_3 = max_reps_in_group >= 2,
    criterion_4 = !seen_in_STY_search,
    passes_all = criterion_1 &
      criterion_2 &
      criterion_3 &
      criterion_4
  )

candidate_check
group_detections

```
It passes two of the categories (its not seen in the STY search and it has a LP >0.75). However it has a Threonine close by and also is only found once in anc_SN. 


#6.3 Where are the phosphosites on the Tier1?

```{r}

# Keep only the strongest-tier histidine sites
strongest_his <- my_tiers %>%

# Standardize protein IDs and retrieve protein lengths
```

for the H18 it seems to be retained across many examples according to Blast. So maybe conserved in ScpA proteins. ## 7. Real or artefact? A decision framework

For each candidate, go through this list and write your verdict in your lab notebook.

1. **Chemistry:** acid-labile pHis + acidic workflow → is it plausible the site survived?
2. **Localisation:** LP ≥ 0.75? Any S/T/Y on the peptide? Same peptide explained by STY?
3. **Reproducibility:** seen in ≥ 2/3 replicates of a group? In more than one group?
4. **Biology:** is the protein a known His-phosphorylated protein? Is the His conserved?
5. **Spectra:** (beyond this course, but name it) inspect the MS2 spectra – are there
   fragment ions that pin the phosphate to H? pHis shows characteristic neutral
   losses (e.g. −80, −98, −116 Da).
6. **Orthogonal validation:** pHis-specific antibodies, non-acidic enrichment, mutation
   of the His.

**Discussion:** after this analysis, how would you phrase our evidence for (or against)
the claim of Prust *et al.*? Distinguish "we found no evidence" from "we found evidence
of absence".
